body:
I’m talking about the classes used to interact with a form on the page.

$form = $crawler->filter(‘form input[type=submit]’)->form();
$form[‘colors[]’] = array(‘red’, ‘blue’, ‘orange’);

On Tuesday, August 2, 2011 at 1:55 AM, odino wrote:

> Hi Kris,
> 
> I've tried:
> 
>  $crawler = new Crawler();
>  $crawler->addHtmlContent('<html><form><select name="select[]"><option>1<option><option>2<option></select></form></html>', 'UTF-8');
> 
>  $this->assertEquals('select[]', $crawler->filter('select')->attr('name'), '->addXmlContent() adds nodes from an XML string');
> 
> and it works, but you are probably referring to another issue: could you be more specific? (sorry :))
> 
> ## 
> 
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub:
> https://github.com/symfony/symfony/issues/1579#issuecomment-1707541

Hi,

I've took a bit of look into this but it seems that the function: https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/master/src/Symfony/Component/DomCrawler/Form.php#L348 should accept an array, so far so good, while https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/master/src/Symfony/Component/DomCrawler/Field/FormField.php#L69 , which is marked with @api, accepts only strings as it does a type cast on the value.

While the fix should be simple, just remove the type cast, it means that it will break the @api notation rules as I understand them.

Maybe @fabpot or someone else here has a better idea?

P.S. I've used this for the test code, could it be I did something wrong in it?

``` php
        $crawler = new Crawler(null, 'http://localhost/demo.html');
        $crawler->addHtmlContent('
        <html>
            <head>
                <title>Demo</title>
            </head>
            <body>
                <form>
                    <input type="text" name="colors[]" value="" />
                    <input type="text" name="colors[]" value="" />
                    <input type="text" name="colors[]" value="" />
                    <input type="submit" value="ok" />
                </form>
            </body>
        </html>
        ', 'UTF-8');

        $form = $crawler->filter('form input[type=submit]')->form();
        $form['colors[]'] = array('red', 'blue', 'orange');

        var_dump($form['colors[]']);
        die();

```

issue.title: [DomCrawler] added support for forms where several fields have the same ...
issue.body:
...name (which also bring us support for fields ending with [])

This change breaks the public API but it was necessary to make the component behave like a normal browser with a PHP backend.

This fixes #1579.

As we break the public API, I would like some feedback before merging it.
